title: Runtime footprint profiles and streaming batch gating for Llama/Mistral/Qwen extended-context
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Produce per-model GPU footprint profiles and a lightweight streaming batch-gating controller that cooperates with continuous batching and KV cache residency heuristics to avoid OOMs and reduce spiky tail latency for 32k+ context workloads (Llama, Mistral, Qwen families).

Background: We continue to see tail OOMs and large variance in per-request latency when long-context requests cluster with short requests under continuous batching. Existing memory heuristics assume static working-set sizes per model variant; this ticket experiments with compact per-model footprint curves (sequence length -> expected resident bytes) plus a streaming gate that delays or reshapes batch admission when estimated resident set threatens GPU capacity.

Deliverables:
- Small-footprint JSON profiles per model-variant (e.g., llama-65b-q8_0, mistral-x-7b-q4, qwen-14b-q5) mapping seq_len percentiles to resident GPU bytes and KV pressure hints.
- A runtime "streaming batch gate" that: (1) consumes incoming requests, (2) consults the profile + current occupancy estimator, (3) either admits immediately, queues to short-hold window, or issues a prefetch/cold-evict hint to the allocator.
- Integration tests + synthetic benchmarks demonstrating 20-40% reduction in tail latency (p95-p999) and elimination of reproducible OOMs for mixed-length traffic.

Constraints & non-goals: This work targets inference workloads on current dedicated GPU pools (A100/H100 types). We are not changing kernel-level allocators or introducing cross-model memory sharing. Aim for conservative gating (favor availability over throughput) in first rollout.

Metrics to track: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, OOM count, average batch admission delay, GPU memory headroom distribution, tokens/sec per-GPU.

Instrumentation & artifacts: Profiles will be stored in /configs/runtime/footprints/{model_variant}.json and surfaced via /internal/footprint-metrics. Benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-bench/tree/feature/streaming-gate. Design doc (initial): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Streaming+Batch+Gate+and+Footprint+Profiles

Rollout plan: canary on one dedicated pool with long-context workload (customer-sim or internal replay) -> monitor headroom + latency -> expand to multi-pool with gradual threshold relaxation.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Confluence. Agreed to target 3 representative variants (small/medium/large) before generalizing. Decided to use percentile-based profiles (5th/50th/95th) instead of single mean value to capture skew.

2026-02-25 - Marco Liu: Lab experiments show that simple linear scaling of resident bytes with seq_len underestimates Mistral's KV overhead at >24k tokens. We captured per-layer KV deltas and produced provisional profiles (see /tmp/mistral-x-profiles.csv).

2026-03-01 - Engineering review (Core Runtime): Reviewed gating API and agreed to expose a non-blocking admit/queue/evict hint surface. Concern raised about scheduler fairness; proposed soft-deadline aging for queued requests to avoid starvation.

2026-03-04 - Perf: Synthetic mixed workload (60% short, 40% long) with streaming gate reduced p999 from 1.8s -> 1.1s and eliminated two OOM reproductions. Throughput dropped ~6% in worst-case conservative thresholds.
2026-03-06 - Design feedback (Priya Patel): UX for console needs an explicit "footprint headroom" chart and per-model profile editor. Added label 'console-integration' to follow-up tickets.
2026-03-09 - Security review request: Confirmed no secrets or PII in profiles; gating logic runs within runtime sandbox. Security accepted minimal risk; no further action required.

2026-03-12 - Marco Liu: Implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298. Includes profile loader, gating controller, and unit tests. Requesting review from @runtime-team and @perf-team. Next: add long-run soak tests and dashboard panels.

2026-03-12 - CI: Flaky test observed in eviction-path unit test under ASAN build. Investigating; likely race in allocator mock when concurrent prefetch hint arrives. Repro steps added to PR description.

2026-03-12 - Product (Elena Voss): Confirmed prioritized customers for canary and will coordinate traffic shaping. We have two pilot customers who've agreed to internal replay datasets for validation.
